stories.title: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, denies Trump got him rehired
stories.summary: In his first all-hands meeting since returning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang apologized to staff, denied reports that Trump and the White House helped reinstate him, and defended skipping a succession plan.
stories.more: At the meeting, Huang apologized for his intense management style and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company, according to Wired. He also pushed back on the narrative, reported by Bloomberg, The New York Times and others, that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, per The Verge. TechCrunch reports Huang thanked the White House and said he is in therapy during the same meeting. He also reiterated his view that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy, a stance TechCrunch notes comes after two weeks in which Nvidia operated without him.

stories.title: Tidal to ban AI-generated music, deleting tens of millions of tracks
stories.summary: Starting December 9th, Tidal will ban fully AI-generated music, deleting an estimated 27-29 million tracks and rejecting tens of thousands of new AI uploads per day.
stories.more: Tidal music lead Robert Andersen says the platform will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 AI tracks per day once the ban takes effect on December 9th, per The Verge. Ars Technica puts the number of tracks to be deleted at 27 million and notes AI songs currently make up 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalog. TechCrunch reports Tidal will still accept songs made with AI assistance, just not those fully generated by AI. The move follows Tidal's earlier step, months ago, of labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as fully AI-generated.

stories.title: Paper proposes 'loom attention' to let transformers rewire circuits per token
stories.summary: Researchers describe loom attention, a mechanism that lets a Transformer dynamically rewire its internal circuits at every token by mixing vertical attention over earlier heads with standard horizontal attention over tokens.
stories.more: Loom attention combines horizontal attention over tokens, as in standard Transformers, with vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads, used to obtain a head's query, key and value. The vertical attention is implemented efficiently using normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores compressed head outputs and acts as a second residual stream. This design, called LoomFormer, is described as a dual-stream architecture. The excerpt cuts off before detailing benchmark results or model sizes tested.
